issues.description: Method signature mismatch for SealSaloon.checkOrderReady: the problem statement (UML and textual API) declares a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void, while the solution implementation defines checkOrderReady with a boolean parameter (public void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)). This creates an API inconsistency: the specification and UML indicate callers should invoke checkOrderReady() without arguments, but the solution both declares the method with a parameter and calls it with a boolean (this.checkOrderReady(true)). Students following the problem statement or tests expecting the no-argument signature will be confused or produce code that does not match the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the SealSaloon API consistent with the problem statement. Option A (preferred): Change the solution to declare a no-argument method: public void checkOrderReady() { ... } — remove the boolean parameter, move or remove any debug logging controlled by enableLogging (e.g., use a private field or conditional local logging), and update all internal calls to this.checkOrderReady() (replace this.checkOrderReady(true) with this.checkOrderReady()). Option B (if the boolean is intentional): update the problem statement and UML to document the boolean parameter (checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging): void) and ensure tests and instructions refer to the parameterized signature. Ensure either approach keeps the method signature in the UML, problem text, and implementation identical.
